Full 3D Hometown buildings: a look test

The Mill, the Kitchen and the house, built as low-poly 3D models in the style of the world's purchased tree and rock pack, and set beside today's painted sprites. The camera is the steep diamond the perspective study recommends: orthographic, looking down 45° from the south-west. The light is today's Hometown sun. The question: does the town go full 3D, or stay with painted billboards?

A look test. Nothing here is in Unity.

At the phone's size

Three buildings touching in a line on the starter lawn, drawn at a point per CSS pixel of a test phone. The images carry three times the pixels, as the phone's screen does. No interface is drawn; the dark bands mark the status bar with its camera hole, and the gesture bar.

Default zoom: 24.4 points a grid cell, the town’s opening view on a 412-point-wide phone.

Closest zoom: 63 points a cell.

Beside today's painted art

Each model and its painting on the same paved plot, at the same scale. The paintings are placed by the perspective study's rule: as wide as the plot on screen, their foot on its middle. They cast no shadow here.

Mill, on its 2 × 2 plot

Kitchen, on its 3 × 3 plot

House, on its 4 × 4 plot

Turned to each side

Each building rotated a quarter turn at a time on its plot. The sun stays put, so the lit walls and the shadows change as a real building's would. A mirrored sprite can't do this.

Touching, as a line

The 2 × 2 Mill, the 3 × 3 Kitchen and the 4 × 4 house with their plots touching. The house's shadow falls across the Kitchen's roof.

The Mill's sails

The sails are their own part and turn about the hub. Their swept circle stays inside the plot's allowance, so they are about two thirds the size of today's painted rotor.

Under today's camera

The same models under today's 35.264° camera, for comparison.

The models

Each is one mesh with one material and a 64-pixel palette texture, as the pack's props are. Every piece is a closed solid of one colour, so no colour edge zigzags across triangles. The check below imports each exported FBX file and measures it; it fails on any breach.

House4 × 42,8084.86 of 5.00.00(0, 0, 0), lowest point 0100, one colour eachHousepasses

The shared palette. Each swatch stores the colour it should show in sunlight, divided by what today's Home light multiplies it by: about 1.3 on a sunlit wall and 1.6 on the roofs. The magenta cells are unused.

Lighting check: the sunlit lawn renders at exactly its target colours (#93C552 and #89B94C), and the shaded lawn at the game's own shadow value (passes).

What the test shows

  • Turning works in 3D. The light and the shadows are right in all four facings, which is what a mirrored sprite got wrong.
  • 3D buildings shade their neighbours and the lawn. A billboard can't.
  • At the default zoom a house is about 140 points wide, and both kinds read. The models look simpler: the paintings' stonework, scalloped tiles and hinges are gone. Single-colour pieces can't carry that detail within the triangle budget.
  • The budget is tight. The Kitchen uses 2,960 of its 3,000 triangles, mostly on the counter's bread, pie and pans.
  • The plot rule shrinks the Mill's sails to about two thirds of the painted rotor. Turned 90° or 270°, the sails are seen nearly edge-on.
  • The models match the world's 3D trees and rocks. The paintings are a richer, different style.
